faq.question: Is Bazi the same as the Chinese zodiac?
faq.answer: No. The Chinese zodiac uses only birth year, while Bazi analyzes year, month, day, and hour for a much deeper life structure interpretation.

faq.question: Can Bazi predict exact future events?
faq.answer: Bazi identifies timing patterns and probabilities rather than fixed events. It reveals cycles of opportunity, pressure, and transformation.

content.text: Bazi, also known as the Four Pillars of Destiny, is a traditional Chinese metaphysical system used to analyze a person's life blueprint based on their birth date and time. The term 'Bazi' means 'Eight Characters,' referring to the eight Chinese characters derived from your birth year, month, day, and hour.

Your birth data is converted into four pillars: Year Pillar, Month Pillar, Day Pillar, and Hour Pillar. Each pillar consists of a Heavenly Stem and an Earthly Branch, forming the eight characters that define your energetic structure.
The Role of the Five Elements

At the core of Bazi analysis are the Five Elements: Wood, Fire, Earth, Metal, and Water. These elements interact in cycles of support and control. The balance between them determines personality tendencies, strengths, weaknesses, and life themes.

The Day Master represents your core self. It is the Heavenly Stem of your Day Pillar and defines your elemental identity. Understanding whether your Day Master is strong or weak is essential for interpreting your chart correctly.

Bazi does not only describe personality. It also tracks 10-year Luck Pillars and annual cycles. These cycles reveal when certain elements become activated, influencing wealth opportunities, career shifts, relationships, or challenges.
Bazi is not about fixed destiny. Instead, it maps energetic tendencies and timing patterns. With awareness, individuals can make strategic decisions aligned with favorable cycles.
